authority: normative; every claim here is verified against its runtime by `saipen policy verify`
why_one_file: The three runtimes answered to three separate prose documents, and nothing checked that they agreed. A reader had to cross-read commands.py, hush.py and response_surface.py to learn whether a mixed command keeps its order. This file is the single machine-readable statement those runtimes must satisfy; prose in EXECUTION.md and CORE.md explains it but is not the authority.

opaque: a plus inside a token (C++ , A+B)

rules.text: a separator run yields no empty segment: repeated newlines, a doubled standalone plus and surrounding blanks all collapse, and an input that is only separators yields no segments
unbalanced quoting makes the whole input unresolvable rather than partially parsed
prose or a handoff is ONE segment, never split on its punctuation
on the CLI argv path an empty segment is a refusal, not a silent drop, because argv already carries shell word boundaries
a segment starting with 'saipen ' is a canonical command
a leading slash before a REGISTRY-declared verb is the documented operator spelling of that verb (/goal == saipen goal); an undeclared verb stays unknown
a whole first token matching the registry shortcut table owns its payload
a bare token that matches nothing is unknown, never a guessed shortcut
no model interpretation exists on this path; an unresolved token fails closed with an empty command

ordering.invariant: resolved segments keep their input index; the index is never renumbered, sorted or merged

stop.rule: under the default, the first failing segment freezes every later segment to NOT_RUN; CONTINUE_WHEN_INDEPENDENT keeps a later segment only when it is provably independent

provenance.invariant: every recognized segment receives an explicit terminal disposition; no segment disappears
forbidden: a segment omitted because a model judged it unnecessary
a later segment running after an earlier failure under the default policy

hush.lifecycle: strip -> resolve -> run -> suppress discretionary -> bounded report -> eject
hush.fail_closed: an output kind outside the mandatory set is treated as mandatory, never as suppressible
hush.skill_mirror_exception: a Skill load announcement is tool plumbing the host emits itself, not agent narration; hush never suppresses host-owned lines

must_hold: ORDERING: the cleanup segment resolves at index 0 and the goal segment at index 1, unchanged
STOP: if the cleanup segment is REFUSED, BLOCKED or FAILED, the goal segment is NOT_RUN under the default policy
PROVENANCE: both segments carry a terminal disposition and neither is dropped
HUSH: a hush modifier suppresses narration only; the mandatory final report and every refusal still print

refuses_when: a declared runtime module or symbol is absent
a declared closed set differs from the runtime's own derivation
the registry block this file defers to disagrees with what the file states
the mixed-command example does not reproduce ordering, STOP and provenance
